exercises.instruction: 33, 34, 35, and 36 Express the integral $$\iiint_{E}{f{\left( {x,y,z} \right)}\mathit{dV}}$$ as an iterated integral in six different ways, where $$E$$ is the solid bounded by the given surfaces.

solution.paragraph: $$\begin{array}{l} {\int_{- 2}^{2}{\int_{0}^{4 - x^{2}}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - x^{2} - y} \slash 2}^{\sqrt{4 - x^{2} - y} \slash 2}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dz}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dx}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{0}^{4}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - y}}^{\sqrt{4 - y}}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - x^{2} - y} \slash 2}^{\sqrt{4 - x^{2} - y} \slash 2}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dz}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{- 1}^{1}{\int_{0}^{4 - 4z^{2}}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - y - 4z^{2}}}^{\sqrt{4 - y - 4z^{2}}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz}}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{0}^{4}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - y} \slash 2}^{\sqrt{4 - y} \slash 2}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - y - 4z^{2}}}^{\sqrt{4 - y - 4z^{2}}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dx}\mathit{dz}\mathit{dy}}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{- 2}^{2}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - x^{2}} \slash 2}^{\sqrt{4 - x^{2}} \slash 2}{\int_{0}^{4 - x^{2} - 4z^{2}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz}\mathit{dx}}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{- 1}^{1}{\int_{- \sqrt{4 - 4z^{2}}}^{\sqrt{4 - 4z^{2}}}{\int_{0}^{4 - x^{2} - 4z^{2}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dy}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dz}}}}}} \end{array}$$

image.alt: Details A three dimensional rendering of a solid is graphed in the first octant of the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes slightly down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The solid, labeled E, has four sides. The base lies on the x y plane and is a right triangle with two linear sides and a parabolic hypotenuse. One linear side lies along the positive y axis and the other runs parallel to the positive x axis. The hypotenuse traces a parabolic path from the origin and opens along the positive x axis. The back face is a right triangle on the y z plane. The front face is a curved triangular plane labeled y = sqrt(x). It begins from a vertical side along the positive z axis and tapers downward to the x y plane. The top face is a curved plane labeled z = 1 minus y. It shares two linear sides with the base and the curved side with the front face.

solution.paragraph: $$\begin{array}{l} {{\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{\sqrt{x}}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1 - y}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dz}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dx}}}}} = {\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{y^{2}}{\int_{0}^{1 - y}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dz}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1 - z}{\int_{0}^{y^{2}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dx}\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz}}}}} = {\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1 - y}{\int_{0}^{y^{2}}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dx}\mathit{dz}\mathit{dy}}}}}} \\ {= {\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{1 - \sqrt{x}}{\int_{\sqrt{x}}^{1 - z}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dy}\mathit{dz}\mathit{dx}}}}} = {\int_{0}^{1}{\int_{0}^{{(1 - z)}^{2}}{\int_{\sqrt{x}}^{1 - z}{f\left( {x,y,z} \right)\mathit{dy}\mathit{dx}\mathit{dz}}}}}} \end{array}$$

image.alt: Details A three dimensional rendering of a solid is graphed in the first octant of the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The solid, labeled E, four sides. The base is a right triangle. One side of the base is along the positive y axis and one side is parallel to the x axis. The two linear sides are along the positive x and y axes between the origin and the tick mark 1 on the axes. The hypotenuse lies between (1, 0, 0) and (0, 1, 0). The back face is a square which lies on the y z plane with its vertices at (0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), (0, 1, 1), and (0, 0, 1). The left face lies on the x z plane and is a right triangle with a parabolic hypotenuse and has its vertices at (0, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), and (0, 0, 1). The front face, labeled y = 1 minus x, is also a right triangle with a parabolic hypotenuse with vertices at (1, 0, 0), (0, 1, 0), and (0, 1, 1) and rises vertically upward from the x y plane. The top surface is a part of the parabola defined by z = 1 minus x^2. It has a linear side on the y z plane, a curve side on the x z plane and another curve side in the first octant.

exercises.instruction: 57–58 Average Value The average value of a function $$f\left( {x,y,z} \right)$$ over a solid region $$E$$ is defined to be $$f_{avg} = \frac{1}{V(E)}{\iiint\limits_{E}{f{\left( {x,y,z} \right)}\mathit{dV}}}$$ where $$V(E)$$ is the volume of $$E$$ . For instance, if $$\rho$$ is a density function, then $$\rho_{avg}$$ is the average density of $$E$$ .

problem.paragraph: Find the average value of the function $$f\left( {x,y,z} \right) = xyz$$ over the cube with side length $$L$$ that lies in the first octant with one vertex at the origin and edges parallel to the coordinate axes.
Find the average height of the points in the solid hemisphere $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} \leqslant 1$$ , $$z \geqslant 0$$ .

list.item: Find the region $$E$$ for which the triple integral $$\iiint\limits_{E}{{({1 - x^{2} - 2y^{2} - 3z^{2}})}\mathit{dV}}$$ is a maximum.

solution.paragraph: The region bounded by the ellipsoid $$x^{2} + 2y^{2} + 3z^{2} = 1$$
